Read a Greenlandic TA file

Source: R/ta.R
read_ta.Rd

Reads a Greenlandic TA file in the old layout (version 1) or the new 140-character layout (version 2), recognising which by itself.

Usage

read_ta(path, version = NULL)

Arguments

path

Path to the TA file.

version

1 (old layout), 2 (new layout), or NULL (default) to recognise it from the file.

Value

A tibble with one column per field: 12 for version 1, 9 for version 2.

Details

The layouts. Character positions, 1-based. Text fields are read as character, the rest as numbers.

FieldVersion 1Version 2Type
nrnr1–51–6text
trans7–1217–21text
brch14–1731–35text
bas19–3136–60number
eng33–4361–76number
det45–5577–92number
afg57–6793–108number
moms69–79109–124number
kbx81–91125–140number
prim93–103number
afstm105–107text
fval109–endtext

Recognising the version. Version 2 lines are 140 characters, with blanks at 7–16 and 22–30, where version 1 has trans, brch and bas. When every line looks like version 2, the file is read as version 2; when none does, as version 1. A mix is an error. Giving version skips the guess, but a file that clearly is the other version is still an error, rather than read into the wrong columns.

Values. Fields are trimmed, and a blank field or NA is read as NA. A number field that is not a number is an error listing every such field, not a silent NA. Empty lines are skipped; line numbers in messages are those of the file.

See also

write_ta()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
df <- read_ta("ta.file")
df <- read_ta("ta.file", version = 2)
} # }
